paragraphs: You begged me not to take this house, and you were right. I am writing by my last candle, so I must be quick.
When I arrived, every portrait in the hall hung upside down. I thought the last family were simply odd, and I set them all right. That night the knocking began inside the walls.

Today I found their diary in the cellar. They turned the portraits so that it could not look out through the painted eyes. Now it watches me from every room, and it comes closer whenever the light grows dim. Last night it knocked ~~twelve~~ thirteen times, then said my name from ~~beside~~ beneath my bed.
Do not come for me. If you must, turn the portraits back over, and whatever you do, do not let your light go out.
postscript: P.S. The candle is guttering. I can see its eyes now, just past the edge of the light.
carvings: I BROKE HER BEFORE I KILLED HER.
SHE FOUGHT HARDER THAN I EXPECTED.
I TOOK MY TIME WITH HER.
I MADE SURE SHE COULDN’T RUN.
SHE CRIED WHEN SHE REALIZED YOU WEREN’T COMING.
